summary: Weeping at the empty tomb, Mary Magdalene meets the risen Jesus, takes Him for the gardener, knows Him when He speaks her name, and is sent to His brethren.
key_insight: Mary did not know Jesus by sight, even face to face. She knew Him when He said one word: “Mary!” Jesus had said that the shepherd “calls his own sheep by name” (John 10:3).
story: But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. As she wept, she stooped down and looked in, and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet. {Jn}
They said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid Him.” {Jn}

Then she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but she did not know that it was Jesus. He said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking?” Supposing Him to be the gardener, she said, “Sir, if You have carried Him away, tell me where You have laid Him, and I will take Him away.” {Jn}
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to Him, “Rabboni!” which means Teacher. {Jn}
Jesus said, “Do not cling to Me, for I have not yet ascended to My Father; but go to My brethren and say to them, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, and to My God and your God.’ ” {Jn}

So it was to Mary Magdalene, out of whom He had cast seven demons, that the risen Jesus appeared first. {Mk} She came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that He had spoken these things to her. {Jn} They were mourning and weeping, and when they heard that He was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe. {Mk}
differences: Mark says in one sentence that Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene; John tells the whole meeting.
Only Mark recalls that Jesus had cast seven demons out of Mary and that the disciples were mourning and weeping.
John says Mary told the disciples she had seen the Lord; Mark adds that they did not believe her.

fit.question: Mark says Jesus appeared “first to Mary Magdalene.” Matthew tells of Jesus meeting the women as they went to tell the disciples (Matthew 28:9; event 180). Who saw Him first?

points.label: Mary on her own
points.text: Mary had run to Peter before the other women heard the angels (John 20:2), and she came back to the tomb after Peter and John had gone. Jesus met her there alone. The other women, on their way with the angels’ message, met Him afterward.

points.label: Matthew does not say when
points.text: Matthew says Jesus met the women on the way, but he does not say that no one had seen Jesus before them. Mark’s “first” and John’s account agree that it was Mary.

fit.note: The accounts allow a clear order: Mary first, at the tomb, then the other women on the way. Nothing here requires an error.
fit.short: Mary, back at the tomb alone, saw Jesus first; the other women met Him afterward on their way to the disciples.

scene.label: The manuscripts
scene.text: The NKJV includes Mark 16:9–20 and notes that some of the oldest manuscripts do not have it.

scene.label: The gardener
scene.text: The tomb was in a garden (John 19:41). A man there in the early morning could easily be taken for the one who looked after it, and Mary thought He might have moved the body.

scene.label: Rabboni
scene.text: This Aramaic word means my teacher or my master, a warmer and more personal form of Rabbi. John translates it for his Greek readers.

scene.label: “Do not cling to Me”
scene.text: Jesus was not forbidding any touch; Matthew says the women held Him by the feet (28:9), and Jesus later invited Thomas to touch His wounds (John 20:27). Most understand Him to mean, Stop holding on to Me: He was not returning to life as it had been, He would ascend to the Father, and Mary had a message to carry.

scene.label: A woman’s witness
scene.text: Courts of the time gave little weight to a woman’s testimony; the Jewish historian Josephus says women should not be accepted as witnesses. A story invented to persuade would hardly make a woman the first witness of the risen Lord.

witnesses.mark: Mark 16:9–11 gives a brief summary: Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, she told the grieving disciples, and they did not believe. It names her as the woman from whom Jesus had cast seven demons, the same Mary who watched at the cross and came to the tomb.
witnesses.john: John tells the meeting in full: Mary’s tears, the angels, the supposed gardener, and the single word that opened her eyes. Here, for the first time in John, Jesus calls His disciples “My brethren” and speaks of God as “My Father and your Father,” the family His death and resurrection created.

seeing.reveals: The risen Jesus knows His own by name. His first appearance was not to Pilate or the priests but to a grieving woman once held by seven demons, and He made her the first messenger of His resurrection.
seeing.living: Jesus now calls His Father “your Father” and His disciples “My brethren.” Those who belong to Him are family, and like Mary they are sent to tell others what they have seen of the Lord.
seeing.ponder: When Jesus speaks your name, what does He find you seeking?

preaching.big_idea: The risen Jesus calls His own by name and sends them to tell His family.
preaching.watch_for: Jesus asks Mary, “Whom are you seeking?” (v. 15), the question He put to the soldiers in Gethsemane (18:4). In His first words to His first disciples He had asked, “What do you seek?” (1:38).
